final_recommendation: The room converged on a fully operationalized risk framework: a consolidated supplier map (due Friday 9 AM) integrating RVC shortfall scores, debt-to-EBITDA ratios, capex headroom, retrofit-versus-relocate costs, audit-hold revenue losses, and keep-versus-exit tier classifications. The 400-bps trade-credit surcharge, 90-day audit-hold sequence, and $2–4M insolvency cost per supplier became priced underwriting factors, not soft flags.

key_concessions: Compliance accepted debt-to-EBITDA >3.5x as the hard insolvency trigger and committed to EOD balance-sheet delivery

downstream_risk_variables: Tier-1/2/3 supplier classification matrix (self-fund / credit-support / co-invest-or-exit)
RVC-shortfall-to-insolvency overlap list with per-supplier capex headroom and nearshoring costs

Days-to-insolvency calculation from audit-hold start date
400-bps trade-credit surcharge retroactive to audit date for RVC-short + leveraged suppliers
78–80% RVC sensitivity range for 2026 review risk
uncertainty_notes: The room did not resolve: (1) which specific tier-2 suppliers are currently RVC-short (awaiting supply chain's 6 PM Thursday delivery); (2) the exact number of suppliers in active RVC audits and their audit start dates (awaiting compliance's audit-status snapshot); (3) whether the 2026 review will actually tighten RVC thresholds to 78–80% (priced as sensitivity, not certainty); (4) how to price business interruption insurance for the 90-day audit hold beyond revenue-loss quantification.
